Initia's Layer-1 mainnet went live April 24, 2025, confirmed by post-launch trading/airdrop activity reported the following day.

The Lava Foundation raised $11 million in a token round (SAFT) announced May 7, 2024, ahead of the network's mainnet and airdrop, independently reported by The Block; the same report also named the Foundation as the sole controller of token sales and roadmap decisions pending a stated future DAO transition.

Lava Network launched its public mainnet on July 30, 2024, with a community-first airdrop of 55 million LAVA tokens and $2 million in initial network incentives, independently reported by The Block.
Mansa raised $3 million in pre-seed equity and $7 million in liquidity funding.
Mansa reported nearly $31 million in processed volume over its first six months.
Neynar announced a prospective Farcaster handoff from Merkle.

Nillion announced a migration from its Cosmos-based chain to Ethereum ("Nillion 2.0"), redefining NIL's utility around staking, node access, and payments, announced January 27, 2026 and independently corroborated as operationally real by Kraken's exchange migration documentation.
Nillion launched its public mainnet on March 24, 2025, following a February 19, 2025 NIL Token Generation Event, corroborated by an independent Messari research report.

An unauthorized market maker's large NIL sale caused a ~50% price crash around November 20, 2025; Nillion responded with treasury buybacks, exchange coordination to freeze accounts, and stated legal action. Recorded as reported_unconfirmed because the counterparty's "unauthorized" status is established only via Nillion's own account, not an independent third-party finding.
unconfirmedNote: The characterization of the market maker's sale as "unauthorized" and the outcome of Nillion's stated legal action against the counterparty were not independently corroborated within the research budget for this batch; the price crash itself is well-documented, but the legal/authorization narrative rests on Nillion's own account as relayed by specialist crypto-news outlets.

evidenceSummary: Nillion raised $25 million led by Hack VC, announced October 30, 2024, reported by CoinDesk.

Nubit repositioned its public messaging around "Bitcoin Thunderbolt," a proposed Bitcoin base-layer soft-fork upgrade, announced March 5, 2025, shifting from a standalone data-availability-layer narrative toward positioning as a core contributor to a broader Bitcoin scaling initiative.
unconfirmedNote: Nubit's own announcement is the only source for this positioning and for the underlying technical claims; whether Bitcoin Thunderbolt has any standing within an actual Bitcoin Core proposal process, and whether it will ship as described, is not independently confirmed.

evidenceSummary: Independent analytics (ChainArgos) and third-party commentary estimated roughly 70% of Pixels-related accounts on Ronin were bots, undermining the reliability of the company's contemporaneous 1 million DAU claim; Pixels acknowledged banning 750,000 accounts in one week.

Pixels migrated from Polygon to the Ronin blockchain and its PIXEL token listed on Binance on February 19, 2024, with independent reporting valuing the project at roughly $2.7 billion FDV the following day.
Pixels raised $4.8 million in a strategic financing round announced February 9, 2024, ahead of its PIXEL token generation event.

Following a reported ~95% PIXEL FDV decline from its 2024/2025 peak, Pixels introduced heavier PIXEL withdrawal fees redirected to stakers, automatic in-game staking, and a new vPIXEL fee-free token, alongside a stated strategic pivot from raw DAU counts toward higher-lifetime-value users.
unconfirmedNote: Reported by a single independent gaming-news outlet; the exact dates/magnitude of the FDV decline and the operational effect of the new fee/staking mechanics were not independently cross-verified within this batch's research budget.

evidenceSummary: Turnkey announced a $15M Series A (closed ~October 2023, announced April 23, 2024) led by Lightspeed Faction and Galaxy Ventures.
Turnkey announced a $30M Series B on June 9, 2025, led by Bain Capital Crypto, bringing total disclosed funding to over $50M.

A borrower (Kinto) on the Wildcat protocol defaulted following an upstream exploit that drained its own lending pools; this was Wildcat's first confirmed default since its 2023 launch. Wildcat stated the loss was isolated to the Phoenix Facility market with no contagion to other lenders/borrowers, and Phoenix lenders expected ~76% principal recovery.
analystInterpretation: Direct test of Wildcat's borrower-level risk-isolation design; the default is itself a negative event (partial capital loss for Phoenix lenders), while the reported containment to a single market is partial evidence in favor of the protocol's structural risk-isolation claim.

evidenceSummary: Zodia Custody secured a Luxembourg CSSF payment institution license (reported June 9, 2026), extending its regulated EU footprint for stablecoin custody/transfer services alongside its existing MiCA license.

Standard Chartered officially announced, and it is confirmed as a fact of record independently reported by both The Block (citing Bloomberg) and CoinDesk on May 18, 2026, that it made a non-binding offer, accepted by other shareholders/noteholders, to acquire the remainder of Zodia Custody's regulated custody business, moving Standard Chartered from majority to 100% ownership of that business. The announcement and shareholder acceptance are confirmed; the acquisition's closing remains a pending, conditional future step, subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions, and is not established as complete as of the research cutoff.

SC Ventures officially and confirmedly announced plans (May 20, 2026) to spin out Zodia Custody's institutional infrastructure/technology platform into a new independent entity, Zodia Solutions, once the Standard Chartered acquisition completes, with Julian Sawyer named as its intended CEO. The announcement of this planned, conditional formation is confirmed; the entity's actual formation and Julian Sawyer's assumption of the CEO role remain pending on the acquisition's still-unestablished closing and are not asserted as complete as of the research cutoff.
